passages.provision_quote: (a) On and after January 1, 2025, an agency responsible for the development or operation of bikeways or highways where bicycle travel is permitted shall not install a new sharrow on a highway that has a posted speed limit greater than 30 miles per hour, except at or near an intersection for the purpose of connecting a Class I, Class II, or Class IV bikeway through the intersection.
passages.note: SB 1216 bars new sharrows on roads over 30 mph and excludes Class III bikeways from Active Transportation Program funding eligibility — a bike-facility safety/design standard, not a statement of how to split investment between roads and other modes.

rows.reasoning: SB 1216 (2023-2024), authored by Blakespear, prohibits new sharrows on highways with speed limits above 30 mph and removes Class III bikeways/sharrows from Active Transportation Program project eligibility. This is a law about how cyclists and drivers share the road and which facility design standards qualify for the program, not a statement of where to focus transportation investment between road capacity and pedestrian, cycling, and transit infrastructure, so no passage establishes a rung.
